text:
oliver: Quick heads-up — saw a 15-25% p99 latency bump on streaming endpoints after yesterday's batching tweak. Looks tied to partial-decode + kernel handoff.

maria: ugh. which tweak specifically? the coalesce-window shrink?

oliver: yes, we tightened coalesce window to 6ms for low-latency, and that increased partial-decode preemption. When a small streaming batch hits a kernel that expects a full block we see a retranscode + KV miss hit.

raj: can you paste the flamegraph link or perf output?

oliver: perf-bot attached the trace: https://perf.redwood/trace/3305012345 (short-lived, payloads ~40-120 tokens). main hotspot: kernel_select() falling back to generic attention kernel 30% of the time for short sequences.

jess: is kernel fallback because quantized path isn't available for that sequence length?

oliver: exact. sequence-length distribution changed due to streaming chunking: more frequent 8-12 token decode slices. Our kernel selector uses a heuristic that prefers fast kernels for >16 tokens.

kai: maybe we should bias selector toward small-kernel implementations when request flagged as streaming. cheap win: add a streaming_hint -> prefer small-kernel.

maria: also saw KV cache warmup delays. partial-decode causes tiny KV instantiations that flush earlier than expected, leading to extra memory churn.

raj: propose short-term mitigation: 1) raise token_budget target for streaming prefetch to 32, 2) increase coalesce window to 8ms for now, 3) force kernel hint for streaming requests. run AB for 4h.

jess: +1. can we emulate in local harness? I can spin up batch-sim with synthetic distribution.

oliver: attached quick repro command: 

```
# stress runner
python -m runtime.tests.stream_stress --model elven-2-quant --chunk-size 10 --arrival-lambda 0.005 --partial-decode
```

perf-bot: Snapshot: before-change p99_stream=142ms, after-change p99_stream=173ms (+22%). KV-miss-rate jumped from 4.2% -> 9.8%.

maria: interesting: KV-miss rate doubling aligns with more partial sends that bypass prefix cache. Might be our prefix-matching TTL for partial chunks.

kai: idea: group partial-decode flows by conversation id for cache affinity. cheap: use a 200ms sticky window to keep KV warm for that session.

jess: thought: that sticky window may increase memory pressure on high-qps hosts. We should gate by per-GPU free-kv capacity.

raj: plan for next 24h: implement kernel-streaming-hint + streaming token_budget=32 + coalesce 8ms rollback as feature flag. Run AB on 10% traffic. Collect p50/p95/p99, KV-miss, kernel-fallback-rate, per-token CPU.

oliver: i've pushed a draft PR with selector flag: 

```
# selector change excerpt
if request.hints.streaming:
    prefer_kernels = small_kernels + prefer_quantized
```

maria: nice. can you add metrics emitted: kernel_choice, fallback_reason, kv_warm_affinity?

oliver: will add. Also logging sample ids for fallback traces.

perf-bot: AB results after 2h on 10%: p99 down to 150ms (from 173), KV-miss 6.1%, kernel-fallback 12% -> 7%. CPU/token +3%.

jess: promising. small CPU regression expected. Does quality change? any decoding artifacts?

oliver: no diff in outputs on our eval prompt suite. small timing jitter but identical decoded tokens on tracked prompts.

maria: next steps: 1) run 24h AB 50% if no regressions, 2) add sticky-KV gated by free-kv, 3) add unit tests for selector when streaming hints present.

raj: and a follow-up: consider adaptive token_budget: lower for short bursts, higher for sustained sessions. Could use EWMA of inter-arrival.

kai: i'll prototype sticky-KV gating in the warmup layer.

oliver: thanks. I'll follow up in PR and drop the perf trace. tagging @eng-oncall in case we need rollback knobs. :thumbsup:
